feasibility_revision: The frozen two-path version 3 stopped before policy inference: all soup approaches passed, but tomato approaches ended 7.9-8.8 cm from their scripted goal, failing the unchanged 2 cm gate. Version 4 is a narrower one-fixed-path feasibility pilot, keeping all four candidate initial states, all appearance/instruction/seed conditions and the same validity thresholds. Failed versions remain preserved. Object XY arrangement is effectively identical across these four LIBERO Object initial states; they vary robot initial conditions, not independent scenes.
software_revision: Version 2 stopped before policy inference because the new render wrapper omitted returning the original sensor image. Version 3 returns the original image and adds a native-observation-preservation regression test; scientific thresholds and state selection unchanged.
instrument_revision: First reference attempt stopped before policy inference because supersampled robot coverage includes mixed object-boundary pixels. Version 2 separately records those pixels and requires exact unambiguous robot-interior RGB, identical depth, and unchanged robot/camera/physics geometry. No image pixels are patched or composited.

primary: For each fixed current appearance, depicted motion and seed, project swapped-minus-original future-cue endpoint changes onto the original soup-to-tomato XY axis. Primary interaction = (soup-instruction change minus tomato-instruction change)/2. Average both current appearances and seeds within each initial state for the one fixed depicted path; bootstrap whole states. Report both noun-specific signs, every factor cell and cream instruction negative control. Do not count seeds as independent states; initial states share one object arrangement.
secondary: cream instruction response to identical visual edits
decoded gripper registration and cue-region reconstruction
stopping: Freeze before reference construction. All four candidates retained in selection records; reject only failed pre-outcome reference/codec/review gates, without replacement. At least three states required. Complete all native/identity/roundtrip controls before donors; any engineering baseline failure stops donor execution. Every included clip needs actual AI-assisted or human review before donor outcomes. No outcome-dependent exclusions or silent restart.
interpretation: Feasibility diagnostic, not a powered confirmatory study. Material assignments are native object-appearance cues; swapping materials across existing UV meshes is not guaranteed to change complete perceived object identity. Robot/camera/physics and unambiguous source robot-interior pixels must remain fixed within each cue pair; mixed object-boundary pixels are recorded separately. A future-only swap conflicts with current appearance; balanced current/future conditions measure rather than eliminate that limitation. Instruction interaction can support instruction-dependent visual-cue use, not isolated object semantics. No task-success claim: physical simulator identities remain original; execute only 32 controls, no replanning.
